# Bad: both quote forms, an escaped single quote, every check family,
# direct launches with combined flags, continuations, and nested shell code.
run run_zsh '
  [[ A == B ]]
  print after-single
'
run run_zsh "
  [[ \"A\" == B ]]
  print after-double
"
run run_zsh 'print '\''quoted'\''; [ A = B ]; print after-escaped'
run /bin/zsh -fc 'emulate -R zsh; test A = B; print after-test'
run zsh \
  -f \
  -c '
  emulate -R zsh
  [[ A == \
    B ]]
  print after-continuation
'
run bash -c 'run_zsh '\''
  (( count > 0 ))
  print after-nested
'\'''
run run_zsh 'grep -qE pattern file; print after-grep'
run run_zsh '! helper-command; print after-negation'
run run_zsh '[[ A == B && C == D ]]; print after-expression'

# Good: the status is final or explicitly handled. Dynamic code, functions,
# and control-flow bodies are outside this guard's documented static scope.
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]] || exit 3; print guarded'
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]] && print conditional'
run run_zsh 'print before-final; [[ A == B ]]'
run run_zsh '(( count++ )); (( count += 1 )); print arithmetic-update'
run run_zsh 'if [[ A == B ]]; then print branch; fi; print end'
run run_zsh 'helper() { [[ A == B ]]; }; print function-definition'
run run_zsh "$program"
run zsh -f -c "$program"
printf '%s\n' 'run_zsh fake-program'

# Bad: a following compound command still discards the assertion's status;
# quoted data containing list operators does not handle a failed command.
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; if true; then print end; fi'
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; helper() { print end; }'
run run_zsh 'grep -q "left||right" file; print end'
run run_zsh 'test A = "left&&right"; print end'

# Good: real list operators following quoted data still handle status.
run run_zsh 'grep -q "left||right" file || exit 4; print end'
run run_zsh 'test A = "left&&right" && print conditional'

# Bad: quoted data in an unrelated heredoc cannot hide a later literal.
cat <<'DATA'
'
DATA
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; print after-data-heredoc'

# Bad: shifts and here-strings do not consume later command strings.
(( value = 1 << 2 ))
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; print after-shift'
read -r value <<< 'data'
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; print after-here-string'

# Bad: tab-stripping and queued delimiters still resume after data.
cat <<-TABS
	'
	TABS
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; print after-tab-heredoc'
cat <<FIRST <<'SECOND'
'
FIRST
"
SECOND
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; print after-queued-heredocs'

# Good: commands inside ordinary data heredocs are not launches.
cat <<'DATA'
run run_zsh '[[ A == B ]]; print data-only'
DATA
